A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiDAR world-model study. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–H, are readable, and the corresponding text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, forecasting, transfer-learning, ablation, and sampling-sensitivity results on nuScenes, KITTI-360, and the authors' indoor dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds temporal-consistency evaluation, additional baseline comparisons, and compression-dependent reconstruction and forecasting analyses.

M1.justification: The Swin-based VAE, conditional flow-matching forecaster, classifier-free guidance, latent rescaling, and representation-alignment procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.3 explains the existing pipeline more explicitly. The temporally modified VAE introduced in v2 serves FVD evaluation, rather than changing the forecasting method.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, KITTI-360, and the same indoor LiDAR collection for semantic forecasting, beam adaptation, and outdoor-to-indoor transfer. The added comparisons and analyses use retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds evaluated ViDAR and Occ4D comparators to the sparse/dense pretraining results previously reported without external comparators in v1 Table 18. The principal semantic forecasting and reconstruction baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FVD evaluation on six-frame, three-second sequences using temporal VAE features and a shuffled-ground-truth control. It also compares forecasting across four compression ratios with a fixed 200-epoch budget. Appendix B revises the reported semantic validation count from 4,216 to 4,219; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends diagnostics of two central properties: temporal coherence, through FVD and shuffled-order ground truth, and compression tradeoffs, through class-specific information loss and downstream forecasting at different compression ratios. Appendix F.3 also reports sensitivity of highly compressed latents to small perturbations. Existing alignment, LoRA, NFE, data-fraction, and sampling analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: The five-seed sampling means and standard deviations are retained in v1 Table 21 and v2 Table 23. Validation-set NLL means and standard deviations likewise remain unchanged in v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 8. No additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises OccWorld FPS from 2.56 to 16.97 and DOME FPS from 0.76 to 5.48, substantially changing the efficiency comparison. Tables 2 and 19 revise 192x reconstruction mIoU from 93.8 to 92.8, with selected per-class changes. At 10% semantic fine-tuning data, full-parameter 1s/3s mIoU changes from 24.69/10.42 to 25.95/11.09. v2 also adds FVD, baseline, and compression-dependent results. These are reported revisions and additions, not established gains from a changed method.

T1.justification: The flow-matching and alignment objectives, latent-similarity definitions, FID/KID formulas, and likelihood derivations remain mathematically unchanged. The new temporal evaluation and compression findings introduce no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The headline inference-speed advantage is substantially reduced: the abstract and contribution summary change the maximum FPS speedup from approximately 28x to 3.9x. The introduction also explicitly limits the foundational dynamics-prior goal to ground vehicles. The principal transferability, label-efficiency, and high-compression contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 adds explanations involving incomplete convergence at low compression and information loss and noise sensitivity at high compression. Appendix G newly interprets low sampling variability as a limitation: conditional forecasts remain relatively fixed despite Gaussian randomness, motivating separate foreground/background control. Existing physical-consistency and indoor-transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that code is released, specifies the absence of kernel fusion or other CUDA acceleration in FPS measurements, and identifies ViDAR's checkpoint as trained on one-eighth of the dataset. It also documents temporal layers for the FVD feature extractor and the existing fidelity extractor's cross-entropy objective. RTX 4090 timing and DynamicCity's 50-step DDIM timing procedure were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, including nuScenes, ViDAR, optical-flow/interpolation research, and embodied planning/navigation works such as OmniEVA, Mem2Ego, and ET-Plan-Bench. These expand introductory context and support the added comparison, while the related-work organization and central research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 applies widespread copyediting and localized paragraph rewrites, expands Section 3.3 into an explicit pretrain–align–fine-tune explanation, and regroups appendix metrics and results. Existing pretraining and NFE material is integrated into the main discussion, and redundant discussion is shortened. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces its FID column with previously reported parameter counts and corrects the NLL direction arrow. The existing FID/KID table and NFE plot move into the main text. New FVD and compression tables are added; Figure 4 gains explicit OccWorld reference lines, and architecture figures receive sizing and caption refinements.

improvement.justification: The temporal-consistency control and compression tradeoff analyses strengthen validation, while clearer explanations, a more explicit diversity limitation, and the moderated speedup claim improve the paper's presentation and qualification. These gains are limited by unreconciled numerical updates: v2 Table 13 implies a 12.43-point low-data gain while the text retains 11.17, and Table 18 retains 93.8 reconstruction mIoU despite 92.8 in Tables 2 and 19.
